description: issue #775: `wait "1.5"` -- a WORD that parses as a number but not a whole one. This is the third arm of `wait`'s `ol-type` tick-count check, sitting between `wait-non-whole` (the number `1.5`) and `wait-non-number-type-error` (the word `"soon"`, which does not parse as a number at all), and it is the arm that pins WHICH value the diagnostic names. Its `every` twin is `every/every-non-whole-word`. `spec/execution-model.md:33-34` makes "words that parse as numbers are accepted where a number is expected" a normative CORE rule, so the word is coerced far enough to be judged non-whole -- but the value the learner actually wrote is a word, so `params.actual` is `word` and `params.value` is the string `"1.5"`, NOT `number`/`1.5`. That is what `repeat "2.5"` reports for the identical situation, so the whole-number forms agree. Before #775 `executeWaitCall` type-checked with `requireNumber`, which pre-coerced the word and left the wholeness check reporting `actual: "number", value: 1.5` -- an implementation could therefore lose the fact that a word was passed and still pass the corpus, because no fixture covered this arm. As with every other failed `wait` validation the `primitive` event is NOT emitted (the pause never runs), only the instruction event precedes the diagnostic, and the span covers just the argument.

diagnostics.message: wait needs a whole number, but got a word.
